newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Taiwan reach aviation agreement.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Taiwan reach aviation agreement.

text.p: The United States and Taiwan have agreed to end restrictions on flights between the two countries, the Transportation Department announced Friday.

The so-called open skies aviation pact, which will not take effect immediately, will lift curbs on passenger and cargo operations, enabling carriers from each country to fly to any city in the other country as often as they wish.
In addition, the department said, the pact allows airlines from each country to fly on to third countries and to market their services jointly in "code sharing" arrangements.
It said the accord with Taiwan, along with similar ones with other Asian nations, would go into effect when enough nations had reached free market pacts to create a regional "open skies" environment.
The United States has already reached free market pacts with Singapore and Brunei, and Washington hopes to hold talks with other countries later, an official said.
These include Malaysia, South Korea and New Zealand.
The official did not say how many free market accords Washington wanted before they would take effect but said there would have to be enough so "beyond rights" were meaningful.
This was necessary, he said, so that a U.S. carrier, for instance, could leap-frog countries, carrying passengers to and from several Asian nations.

Next Monday, the United States and Japan will take up a Northwest Airlines Corp. complaint that Japan violated the existing U.S.-Japanese aviation agreement by denying Northwest permission to fly a new Seattle-Osaka-Jakarta service, the official said.
Northwest filed the complaint last July and because no progress had been made to resolve the dispute, asked the department last month to take sanctions against Japan.
The department said no action would be taken pending the talks, scheduled to run through Thursday.
Northwest had said that appropriate action would be to deny a request by Japan Airlines Co. Ltd. for new passenger-cargo flights from Tokyo to Kona, Hawaii.
The talks next week would also continue what the United States calls the "exploratory process" to see if there was enough agreement to warrant talks on a free-market aviation services agreement.
Japan has said it wanted a new aviation accord, but the United States has replied that a new pact would not be possible until Japan was in full compliance with the existing agreement.
